submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole detects English prose that describes the physical world: chemistry, physics, materials and engineering text about substances, forces and energy (atom, molecule, bond, carbon, hydrogen, alloy, polymer, charge, voltage, temperature, light). Its strength builds across such a passage and peaks on the words that state an amount, degree or comparison (four, two, three, each, all, both, several, many, high, low), while it stays near zero on narrative, dialogue, clinical, legal, economic, mathematical and humanities prose, on code and on non-English text, even where those carry the same numerals and determiners.

rival_explanations: It is a measurement-and-comparison detector that fires wherever prose states amounts, degrees or comparisons (numerals, quantifiers such as four/two/all/each, scalar words such as high/low), in any expository register, so a clinical, economic or statistical passage dense in figures should fire as readily as a chemistry one.

It is a chemistry-and-materials topic detector restricted to that vocabulary (atoms, molecules, bonds, polymers, alloys), so physics, astronomy and earth-science passages should stay quiet and only chemistry-flavoured wording should fire.

readings.explanation: This pole detects English prose that describes the physical world: chemistry, physics, materials and engineering text about substances, forces and energy (atom, molecule, bond, carbon, hydrogen, alloy, polymer, charge, voltage, temperature, light). Its strength builds across such a passage and peaks on the words that state an amount, degree or comparison (four, two, three, each, all, both, several, many, high, low), while it stays near zero on narrative, dialogue, clinical, legal, economic, mathematical and humanities prose, on code and on non-English text, even where those carry the same numerals and determiners.

It is a measurement-and-comparison detector that fires wherever prose states amounts, degrees or comparisons (numerals, quantifiers such as four/two/all/each, scalar words such as high/low), in any expository register, so a clinical, economic or statistical passage dense in figures should fire as readily as a chemistry one.

It is a chemistry-and-materials topic detector restricted to that vocabulary (atoms, molecules, bonds, polymers, alloys), so physics, astronomy and earth-science passages should stay quiet and only chemistry-flavoured wording should fire.
